architecture ui  ui contributor shared/libs/ui  only the architect may modify this document. fundamental principle  **absolute, hermetic separation between structure and appearance.** ascii | concern | owns | lives in |
|---------|------|----------|
| **markup** | positioning, flow, semantic identity, flags | components, layouts, pages |
| **theme** | every visual property: color, border, radius, shadow, spacing, typography, transitions, opacity, cursor, effects | one theme object per product | visual primitives  everything rendered on screen is one of five primitives: ascii | primitive | what | morphological families |
|-----------|------|----------------------|
| **rectangle** | bounded region with boundary + interior | surface, overlay, control, control group, field, list, layout |
| **vector graphic** | icons, svgs, logos, decorative shapes | shape |
| **media** | images, video, embedded content | media |
| **typography** | styled text | not a family (see below) |
| **animation** | transitions, keyframes, motion | cross-cutting — applied via tokens | morphological families  every visual element belongs to one family. all share the same base token shape (**surfacecontainertokens**). some extend it. the element → family map is `shared/libs/ui/types/elements.ts`, one line per element, and it also says which elements have `sizes` (scale). the theme types, the engine and the components derive from it. ascii | # | family | attribute | prefix | examples |
|---|--------|-----------|--------|----------|
| 1 | surface container | `element` | `surface` | card, panel, section, header, footer, badge, avatar, tile, alert, separator, panel-header, panel-content, panel-footer, progress, spinner, skeleton |
| 2 | elevated overlay | `element` | `overlay` | dialog, drawer, panel-overlay, popover, tooltip, toast, hamburger-menu |
| 3 | interactive control | `element` | `control` | button, icon-button, chip, toggle, switch, checkbox, radio, tab-trigger |
| 4 | interactive control group | `element` | `control-group` | topbar, navbar, sidebar-nav, tab-bar, breadcrumb, pagination-bar, button-group, toggle-group |
| 5 | field | `element` | `field` | input, textarea, select, combobox, date-picker, otp |
| 6 | list container | `element` | `list` | table, list, accordion, menu, tree-view |
| 7 | shape | `element` | `shape` | icon, svg, logo, decorative |
| 8 | media | `element` | `media` | image, video, embedded |
| 9 | layout | `layout` | — | shell, shell-side-nav, shell-top-nav, shell-none, page, page-header, second-page-header, page-body, left-sidebar, main, main-header, second-main-header, main-body, container, context-panel, right-sidebar, scroll-area | morphological families › family-specific extensions  ascii | family | extra tokens beyond surfacecontainertokens |

| elevated overlay | scrimcolor, scrimopacity, scrimblur, entrance/exit animation |

| layout | (no extensions — uses surfacecontainertokens directly) | morphological families › two attributes: `element` and `layout` `element` = morphological identity (what this surface is) `layout` = structural region (where this sits in the page) both are themed identically by the cascade engine. the separation exists because they are different concerns: layout is the frame, element is the surface inside it. a dom node carries **either** `element` or `layout`, never both. morphological families › part attribute `part="name"` marks a structural sub-region inside a themed ancestor. it goes on plain divs that need designer-controlled spacing, gap, or background without carrying a full element identity. only parts explicitly declared in the theme's `parts` field for that surface produce any css — undeclared parts are invisible to the engine. a node never carries both `part` and `element`/`layout`. not implemented in the engine today; the engine knows only its own zones, `data-part="start-icon" | "end-icon" | "thumb" | "scrim"`. the universal shape: surfacecontainertokens every property is optional. only define what you customize. every family uses the same base token structure: boundary         border (width, style, color, per-side), radius (all, per-corner),

interior         background, backgroundalpha, foreground, opacity,

cursor           css cursor value
smartbleed       false | 'normal' | 'rounded' | 'border' | 'border-rounded'
transition       duration, timing

states           hover, active, focus, selected, disabled, loading
status           neutral, error, warning, success, info, destructive
emphasis         hero, primary, secondary, tertiary, quiet typography **default typography (on surfaces):** surfaces that contain text use `defaulttypography` to point at a root type scale. changes per size variant. color comes from `interior.foreground`, never from typography. **typography in markup:** multiple text styles inside a container use `element="type--heading2"`, `element="type--bodysmall"` etc. **18 root type scales:** heading1–4, bodyextralarge–bodyextrasmall, quotelarge–quotesmall, code, numbersextralarge–numbersextrasmall. typography is **not a family**. handled two ways: the cascade  a designer builds incrementally. each level only declares what it changes: ascii | level | what | selector |
|-------|------|----------|
| l1 | primitives | `:root` vars |
| l1b | modes + derivations | `:root` / `[data-mode]` vars |
| l2 | family defaults | `[element^="{prefix}--"]` or `[layout="..."]` |
| l3 | element overrides | `[element="{prefix}--{name}"]` |
| l4 | concept overrides | `[concept="x"] [element="..."]` |
| l5 | contextual overrides | `[element="a"] [element="b"]` | the cascade › overlay axes (compose with any level)  ascii | priority | axis | values |
|----------|------|--------|
| 3 (highest) | state | hover, active, focus, selected, disabled, loading |
| 2 | status | neutral, info, success, warning, error, destructive |
| 1 (lowest) | emphasis | hero, primary, secondary, tertiary, quiet | priority is the author's: the engine emits the `combined` entries of a surface in the order they are written. write emphasis first, then status, then state, if that is the priority you want. the cascade › scale (structural, not an overlay)  `scale` adjusts padding, typography, icon size. never colors. values: xs, sm, md, lg, xl. only elements with `sizes: true` in the elements table can be authored per scale; the engine emits `[element=…][scale=…]` from an element's `sizes`, never at family level, never inherited from a parent. the cascade › concepts concepts work identically for elements and layouts. product-specific semantic identity. a concept wraps elements and overrides their visual treatment. grouped by concept in the theme: concepts: {
  knowledge: {
    card: { accent: 'brand-2', ... }
  },
  dashboard: {
    maincontent: { interior: { background: 'gray-50' } }
  }
} typescript tint mechanism emphasis defines a **pattern** (filled, outlined, ghost) and sets `tint` status overrides `tint` to recolor the pattern properties reference `'tint'` or `'smart-bw'` — they adapt automatically primary button: `tint='brand-1'`, `bg='tint'`, `fg='smart-bw'` → blue filled. primary + error: status overrides `tint` to red → red filled, same pattern. **smart-bw:** auto-picks black or white based on resolved background lightness. prevents combinatorial explosion of emphasis + status combinations. smart bleed  a theme-driven mechanism where a child element extends its background into the parent's padding/border area. resolved at build time — the engine computes the parent's padding/radius from the cascade and emits concrete negative margins. ascii | value | behavior |
|-------|----------|
| `false` | off |
| `'normal'` | bleeds over padding, outer corners rounded, inner edges straight |
| `'rounded'` | bleeds over padding, all corners rounded |
| `'border'` | bleeds over padding + border, outer corners rounded, inner edges straight |
| `'border-rounded'` | bleeds over padding + border, all corners rounded | color system **derivations (computed by engine):** gray-50–950 (from bg↔fg), gray-pure (mode-independent), brand-n-gray-step (tinted grays), brand-n-light/dark, status-x-light/dark, smart-bw, tint. **modes:** light, dark, lowcontrastlight, lowcontrastdark. each defines background/foreground anchors and derivation parameters. not separate themes — transforms on the same primitives. **primitives:** main (white/black), brand (1–4), status (success/info/warning/error), flat (11 accent colors), semantictokens (primary/secondary/accent/muted). css ownership one generated file per theme. one import in the app. the engine generates: @font-face, primitives, modes, tailwind registrations, base layer, cascade rules, component overrides. if the theme isn't loaded, there's no visual identity. correct behavior. no other library, module, or app emits visual css. the theme engine is the **single owner** of all visual css. authority  only the architect may change this document or make architectural decisions. unreviewed unreviewed unreviewed

theme engine ui  ui contributor shared/libs/ui  how the css engine works. the engine compiles a theme object into a single css file that owns all visual styling for the application. architecture  shared/libs/ui/web/theme-engine/
├── conventions.ts     family prefixes, element→family mapping, selector generation
├── emit.ts            token-to-css emitters (boundary, interior, typography, etc.)
├── theme-process.ts   main engine: walks theme, generates complete css output
├── build.ts           build script: imports theme, runs engine, writes css file
├── index.ts           barrel export
├── fonts/             font files (owned by the lib)
├── generated/         output css (one file per theme)
└── sandbox/           visual test page convention-driven the only structural knowledge is in `conventions.ts`: **family_prefixes** — 9 entries mapping family keys to css prefixes **element_families** — maps each element key to its family **family_defaults** — sensible defaults per family (cursor, transition) add an element to the theme → the engine processes it automatically. no registry to update. the engine has no hardcoded element lists. it walks the theme object dynamically and processes whatever it finds. hybrid css approach these exist because tint, smart-bw, and alpha mixing require cross-property composition that plain css properties can't express. **everything else is plain css.** padding, border-width, radius, shadow, cursor, transition, typography — set directly on cascade selectors. no indirection, no variable chains. the engine uses **5 css custom properties** for composition: `--bg`, `--fg`, `--tint`, `--border-color`, `--bg-alpha`. output structure **@font-face** — font file declarations **tailwind variant declarations** — `@custom-variant dark` **l1: primitives** — `:root` custom properties (colors, typography, spacing, etc.) **l1b: modes + derivations** — per color scheme (`:root` default, `[data-mode]` others) **tailwind token registrations** — `@theme inline` block **legacy bridge** — shadcn compat vars (removed as components migrate) **base layer** — `@layer base` (body bg/fg, border defaults) **property application** — tint/alpha composition on `[element]` and `[layout]` **family & element extras** — scrim, placeholder, scrollbar, disabled, icons **cascade** — l2 families → l3 elements → l4 concepts → l5 contextual → axes → sizes **component overrides** — `[data-slot]` integration (removed as components migrate) the generated css file reads as a coherent document: build pipeline the app wears exactly one theme@version, chosen in `configs/theme/index.ts` (`app_theme = { theme, version }`); its vite config aliases `@theme` to that version's generated css: watch mode: `pnpm theme:watch` — rebuilds on theme or engine file changes. npx tsx shared/libs/ui/web/theme-engine/build.ts bash @import "@theme-fonts";
@import "@theme";   /* → shared/libs/ui/themes/wireframes/v2/generated/wireframes.css */ css reads every `themes/<theme>/v<n>/theme.ts`, runs the engine, writes `themes/<theme>/v<n>/generated/<theme>.css` (+ `<theme>-fonts.css`) beside it. smart bleed (build-time resolution)  when the engine encounters `smartbleed` on a contextual child, it resolves the parent's padding/radius/border-width by walking the cascade (l2→l3→l4), then emits concrete negative margins and border-radius values on the child's specific selector. no css variables, no runtime computation. what the engine does not do no runtime javascript in the browser no shadow dom isolation no pr layout class generation no runtime linting no component modifications unreviewed unreviewed unreviewed

naming ui  ui consumer shared/libs/ui  how application components, and their files, are named. this covers the components an app or a slice writes. the library's own elements (`alert-dialog`, `date-picker`) keep the names of the elements table. the rule the file has the component's name: `sidebarshell.tsx` holds `sidebarshell`. one component per file. not every component has a suffix. a component that is one of the roles below takes that role as its last word, as **subject + role** in pascalcase (`orgmemberspage`, `twofactorcard`). a component that is none of the roles has a plain name with no suffix (`avatar`, `badge`, `orgswitcher`). the roles  ascii | role | what it is | example |
|---|---|---|
| `page` | a route's screen | `orgmemberspage` |
| `shell` | the outermost frame the app owns. there are two: `sidebarshell` (`shell-side-nav`) and `nonavshell` (`shell-none`) | `sidebarshell` |
| `layout` | the structure of a page inside a shell: the header, an optional left panel, the main column | `settingslayout` |
| `sheet` | a side overlay | `editmembersheet` |
| `modal` | a centered overlay | `removemembermodal` |
| `toast` | a transient message | `toast` |
| `form` | inputs and a submit | `profiledataform` |
| `list` | a vertical collection | `invitationslist` |
| `table` | a table | `memberstable` |
| `card` | a self-contained surface | `twofactorcard` |
| `tile` | a small, clickable summary block in a grid | `organizationtile` |
| `header` | the top band of a page, card or section | `titleheader` |
| `footer` | the bottom band of a page, card or section | `cardfooter` |
| `panel` | a bounded region beside or within the main content | `filterpanel` | a word that is not in the table is not a role. add the role here first, then use it. shell and layout a `layout` sits inside a shell and builds the page region tree (`page › pageheader + pagebody › [leftsidebar] + main › container`). it is that tree with the header and the left panel as its slots. a page does not build its own layout. `layouts.md` defines a shell as the outermost viewport frame, with three variants (`shell-side-nav`, `shell-top-nav`, `shell-none`). a product uses the variants it needs; ours uses `shell-side-nav` and `shell-none`, so it has `sidebarshell` and `nonavshell` and nothing else is called a shell. where components live  a component several slices use is an app component, in `apps/main/shared/web/src/components/`. a slice does not import it: the app injects it at mount, as it injects `toast` and the router (`scaffolding-and-import-boundaries`). unreviewed unreviewed unreviewed
